utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. The Chamber apologises for the late start. It's not the snow but rather the small remainders of flu, et cetera, which caused us to start a bit late. Mr. Hannis, are you ready to continue? Ms. Hanson, when you need a break, please stop me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We left off yesterday, Your Honour, we'd finished tab 144. I'm inviting Ms. Hanson to go to a new topic. In your report, you talk about Crisis Staffs being involved with the Territorial Defence as before the VRS was formed in May of 1992. And tab 145, Your Honours, I don't intend to put this up on Sanction. This is an exhibit in Mr. Treanor's material. This is master tab 242. This was just the constitution. And Article 110 was what you wanted to refer to there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which relates to --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Article 110 of the constitution of the RS. Is it possible for me to have the binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sure. We should give you your hard copy of binder number 4.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mandates municipalities to set up, organise, and manage the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's the wording. But it's to municipal authorities, the municipality as a body. But, as we know, the Crisis Staffs took over all authorities of the municipal assembly. Yes, it is the right and obligation of municipalities to set up and organise the national defence and to manage the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I want to go to tab 146 in the presentation binder, master tab 101. Could you tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This and the next series of documents are examples of Crisis Staffs setting up TOs, issuing orders to TOs, appointing the commanders, all consistent with the constitution and consistent with the 19 December instructions which said fill up the reserves of the TO and organise defence. So this document is a decision of the Crisis Staff of Bihac of 3 May 1992, appointing the TO commander, the deputy commander, and the chief of staff of what they call the 1st Brigade of the Serbian municipality of Bihac. I would also draw your attention to the letterhead which reads: "The Serbian municipality of Bihac and the Bihac SDS municipal board," but it's issued by the Crisis Staff commander indicating the overlap between the SDS, the Crisis Staff, and the municipality as a whole. This is often seen in Crisis Staff documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does that one reflect the relationship between the Crisis Staff and the TO?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It shows that the commander of the Crisis Staff is appointing the TO commander, which I take to be a sign -- indication of its authority over the TO and its role in setting up the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last item, does it make reference --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, item number 5. "The brigade commander shall receive all commands and tasks from the Bihac SDS municipal board Crisis Staff." So the Crisis Staff is issuing all commands to the brigade command, and the Crisis Staff itself is identified as SDS municipal board, but also municipality at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one question in this respect. I didn't find the words "TO," but that's in the heading above.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's only in the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As another example of a Crisis Staff ordering the military unit, can I refer you to presentation tab 147, master tab number 248, and ask you to tell us about that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that we have two documents under 146. Has that got any specific reason? I also find a decision of the 4th of June, or is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that may have occurred that -- these documents are -- some documents are entered as a range, two documents together. It seems that's how it entered the system, the two pages as one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not intending to talk about this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's surplusage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We would move to presentation tab 147, master tab number 248.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the commander of the Crisis Staff of Bosanska Krupa, dated the 5th of April, 1992, and it is an order that the brigade commander -- I'm reading item 2 here, "the brigade commander, battalion commanders, commander of the TO staff, police commander, and operational duty officer are ordered not to leave their place of residence and to report to the Crisis Staff headquarters every two hours." So an indication of reporting -- the Crisis Staff is commanding the TO and expecting reporting from the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Presentation tab 48 next in the binder, master tab 252.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision of the provisional government of Zvornik - yes, two copies are actually necessary - dated the 18th of April, 1992, on forming a special unit of the Territorial Defence, saying that the seat of this special unit shall be in Karakaj, in the standard -- the premises of the firm Standard. The tasks of the special unit shall be "to secure the territory of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik and other duties determined by the government of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik." So provisional government setting up a special unit and saying that it shall be giving the tasks and duties to that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next two, I believe, also relate to Zvornik. Presentation tab 149, master tab 416.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's two documents. The first one is the provisional government dismissing people from the command of the Zvornik Territorial Defence. This is a decision dated the -- published in the Official Gazette of Zvornik on the 28th of April, but it's referring to a decision apparently brought on the 10th of April. But we see they dismiss, and then the next document is them appointing other members. So the provisional government, as we see here, had the power to dismiss members of the TO command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And next, presentation tab 150 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Terribly sorry, terribly sorry to interrupt you. Regarding number 149, just one small precision, if I may. I'm wondering about number 126: [In English] ... war front. [Interpretation] Could you please explain that sentence and perhaps give us the explanation or make a comment regarding that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You referred to the left-hand side of the page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see the sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. First, I would like to say that this document is a reproduction of -- a translation of the page from the Official Gazette of the municipality of Zvornik, where different decisions would appear, one on the left-hand side of the page and one on the other, so this is a part of a different decision, an earlier decision, if you understand that. What I would take that to mean, I've seen much such similar references in Crisis Staff documents, and I believe they refer to a process known as asanacija, the cleaning up after a battle, removal of dead bodies and dead animals, after the battle is over, the clearing up of the terrain. I see many such discussions. But it's not part of this actual decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we point out that the transcript got -- Judge Hanoteau's point clearly related to point number 126. In fact, it is 26, just in case that ever gets missed later, it could be confusing. Judge Hanoteau's point clearly related to number 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, regarding that particular item, is that often referred to as sanitation as opposed to clearing up?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, asanacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I began to ask you about tab 150 in the presentation, master tab 253.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply in conjunction with the previous decision, this is a decision of the provisional government forming the TO command. So in the previous decision, they dismissed people and appointed others. They, under number 1, appointed as commander of the Territorial Defence staff is Marko Pavlovic, and it's dated the 28th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was there some recognition of this process that was going on at the municipal level, was that recognised at a higher level. Let me refer you next to tab 151. And I think you have an excerpt from that document. It's master tab number 255, and it's the combat readiness report for the VRS that was published in April of 1993. Can you tell us what page you're going to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 10 of the translation; in the original, 00607349, I believe, to begin with. I'm just checking for the original passage, but I'm sure it's -- yes, it's the third paragraph from the top in the B/C/S. It's at the bottom of page 10 in the English. This, as you said, is the report of the VRS itself, describing the first year of the conflict, so I think it's important to see the army's account of the development in this period. "The control and command function in the framework of the establishment of the army of Republika Srpska developed in two stages: The first from 1st April to 15 June, and the second from that date until today. An important development in the first period was the self-organising of municipal and other regional units on the basis of Territorial Defence units under the political and patriotic influence of the Serbian Democratic Party."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you have another excerpt you wanted to highlight at page 13 in the English?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Page 13 in the English; in the B/C/S, it is 00607351. At the beginning -- middle of the page, the middle of the section on infantry units: "The infantry units, which, through self-organisation, grew on a massive scale out of the Territorial Defence and other units, were used only at the beginning of the war according to the decisions of Crisis Staffs and similar authoritative bodies."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there anything additional from that document at this time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, the next -- the first sentence of the next paragraph is also -- it simply continues the story. "When the army of Republika Srpska was formed, these units were incorporated into it. In places where there were no units of the former JNA to serve as a basis for the formation of new units, they were the foundation for the establishment of infantry units." These passages, I think, give a good summary of what I've been trying to show with the documents. Where there was a JNA, in some places, that was the basis for the future army; in other places, the SDS led the organisation of units which were later -- I'm sorry, which were commanded at the beginning by Crisis Staffs and similar bodies, and later formed the basis for the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And particularly during the time between the outbreak of the conflict in early April and the formation of the VRS in the middle of May, did you see other examples of local Crisis Staffs trying to handle the military units in their areas?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see different exertions of authority over these units during this time period of the takeovers or from Crisis Staffs declaring themselves to be municipal authorities and before the formation of the VRS. We see examples of Crisis Staffs ordering and managing -- claiming influence over these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me start out by, then, asking you about the next tab, presentation number 152, master tab number 198. First of all, can you tell us where that document comes from? And then direct us to the highlighted portion you want to discuss.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document comes from Bratunac. It is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Bihac, which Bratunac fell under, dated the 29th of April, 1992. This document is interesting for -- both for its preamble, I would draw your attention to the preamble which says: "That person went to the decision of the National Security Council, the crisis --" so you see that the regional Crisis Staff is basing its action on the decision of the republican level. And then on item 3 on the next page in the translation, it's an order on -- the decision declaring a state of war, and then specifying that "mobilisation shall be carried out by municipal staffs, and all units, including the existing military ones, shall come under the command of the municipal Crisis Staffs and the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Bihac." I note this is dated the 29th of April, two days before the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had been declared, and the status of the JNA in Bosnia was now thrown into question. So we see a regional Crisis Staff saying that all -- even existing military units shall come under the command of the municipal Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that would seem to include JNA units.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you next about presentation tab 153, master tab number 275.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the War Presidency of Bosanska Krupa, dated the 24th of April, 1992, an order to the command of the 1st Krajina Brigade to destroy three bridges. I would note here that this is explicitly an order, and yesterday, Your Honours noted that a similar document, a month later, was called a recommendation. I think that gives an indication of the transition from earlier, Crisis Staffs and similar bodies directly commanding in some places to a recommendation, more emphasis on coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And related to this particular document, that municipality --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, this is Bosanska Krupa, and they're ordering the brigade to destroy three bridges. You will recall Vjestica's remarks at the 12th of May Assembly session, specifying that they had destroyed certain bridges and were planning to destroy others.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to go to presentation tab 154, master tab number 142.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- these are pages from the diary of Nedeljko Rasula, the president of the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most, in particular, the session of the Sanski Most SDS municipal committee of the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you direct us to the excerpt you want to talk about?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 19 in the translation -- starting on page 19, excuse me. The heading is "The Course of Action in Taking Over Power and Establishing the Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where is that in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the B/C/S, it is on 01369256. Under item 4 on that list, on the next page in the translation, it says: "The Crisis Staff, consisting of the following members, shall be in charge of all actions." And it's notable that the second listed member of the Crisis Staff is Colonel Nedeljko Anicic. And as the plan indicates in its -- in the following pages, that page and the next, it includes the brigade being ready, ordering readiness of the brigade, presumably to assist in the action. I don't see that next page in the translation. But it's clear that the Crisis Staff is coordinating with the military on the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If next we could go to tab 155, master tab number 244.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request -- a letter, a letter from Ratko Adzic, assigning himself here as commander of the Ilijas VSN BiH. At the letterhead, we can see it's the Ilijas Serbian army command. I would point out that the initials VSN in Serbian would be -- the phrase army of the Serbian people, Vojska Srpskog Naroda, would have the initials VSN. It's not explicated what the VSN means there. But in the letterhead, Serbian army command. Dated the 12th of June, 1992. It is addressed to the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of BiH. He's informing the president on the situation on the ground and requesting three to five tanks and three self-propelled anti-aircraft guns in order to cleanse certain pieces of terrain in the Ilijas municipality. So we see here that Ratko Adzic is also the president -- he's also the president of the Crisis Staff of Ilijas. We see him here calling himself commander of the army, and requesting tanks and aircraft guns for clearing the municipality. The original word is "da ocistim," that I might clear or cleanse. It's a different form of the verb that we see as asanacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do we see other examples of Crisis Staff members or Crisis Staff heads also taking a role and commanding military forces?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We've seen some documents already where they assign themselves as commandant, commander, which you will recall is the term used in the 19 December instructions. We also have Crisis Staff heads themselves describing their authority over military and civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I want to take you to presentation tab 156, master tab 223. This is a video of an interview of Jovan Tintor.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovan Tintor was president of the Vogosca Crisis Staff, and a member of the SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And before we start to play this intercept, a couple things. Can you tell us who the interviewer was in this --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is from a television broadcast from 1994, a show hosted by Risto Djogo, called "My Guest, His Truth," and it's an interview of Jovan Tintor covering the foundation of the SDS through the war. So I made three excerpts of what I thought were the most relevant comments from Jovan Tintor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before we begin to play those excerpts, can you direct the Court and counsel to the page in the hard copy English translation where we're starting?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're starting on page 7, 7 on to 8 is the first passage. I'm afraid it will take me a moment to find the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We note that we don't have a hard copy English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll see if we can get one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The B/C/S begins on 00255238. I can give them --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Should we put the English up on the ELMO? I don't know what helps the booth the most.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Risto Djogo: And then, you were the president of the Crisis Staff Vogosca. Jovan Tintor: Yes, I was the commander of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We seem to have a technical problem. As soon as we switch on the microphone, we can't hear the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps -- I know before we've tried to play intercepts and other things completely through. I don't know if we could adopt a procedure for this one, because I think we're capable of pausing, if we could just pause every so often and have the interpreter interpret the last speech, the last sentence or whatever, and then continue once they've finished. I don't know if that will work.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There's no problem any more. It seems to be solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Should we start at the beginning again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Jovan Tintor: Yes, I bought that uniform by myself in Novi Sad. Risto Djogo: Then, you were the president of the Crisis Staff Vogosca. Jovan Tintor: Yes, I was the commander of the Crisis Staff that was superior to the military and civil authorities at the time. I took the job very seriously and understood what had to be done at that time. Because, you know that the war in Sarajevo started on the 6th of April. We seized our weapons, the people received their specific tasks, and of course, I went, along with my people, with my units there where the Serbian territory is to defend it and to establish the absolute peace and authority on our territory. However ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you want to make any comment on that excerpt?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He makes a clear statement that as commander of the Crisis Staff, he was superior to military and civil authorities, and he led his units "to establish authority on our territory." The next passage begins at the bottom of the same page in the English translation, and in the B/C/S, it starts about one-third of the way down page 0 -- the next page, 00255238. I'm sorry -- forgive me, 5239.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll play that one now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Jovan Tintor: Well you see, when the war already begun ... I didn't have two minutes of military education, but I put myself at the head of these people as commander and a kind of a civilian leader. I took a rifle and organised the people the best I could. The front line I held was big. It wasn't only Vogosca. I believed that I should help all the Serbs living on the territories where they weren't properly connected, so I held 64 kilometres of the front line. From the Jezero hospital ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, a clear statement of his military as well as his civilian authority. And the extent of the front, he's speaking of himself holding, obviously his units holding a large front line, so a clear military role. Next passage begins at the bottom of that same paragraph, still on page 8 in the translation, and on the following page in the B/C/S, 00255240, about one-third of the way down that page in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll play that one now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "... I was informed ... I was at a meeting in Vrace where Mr. Kukanjac was to be present too. I wasn't so lucky to meet him at that occasion, but I met our present -- our current General Subotic, President Karadzic, President Krajisnik, Mico Stanisic, Momcilo Mandic ... on that meeting we discussed about joining up in order to cut the city in two and, well, to enter the city. Across that bridge, the former Bratstvo i Jedinstvo. Risto Djogo: The bridge of the Serbian warriors. Jovan Tintor: The bridge of the Serbian warriors, to connect -- to join up by using the bridge and to go into the direction of the Vrbanja bridge. Of course, I had an order, well, actually, it was just an agreement to take the military hospital as well and to join up that way also. I was given these instructions and they told me: 'You go to Zuc and wait for the command. Join up with Pofalici, and when you receive the order, Mr. Kukanjac will give the order, then you will go down and cut the city in two. In that way, we will establish contact with both Serbian sides.' And I personally believe, that if we did it then, the war would have stopped right away. Sarajevo would be divided in two enclaves ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any comment on that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also interesting, not just for his assertion of his military role but for his description of going to a meeting with Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik, as well as other leaders, Stanisic and Mandic, discussing how to divide Sarajevo in two militarily. He says: "I was given an order," and then he corrects himself to an agreement, which implies the meeting had some discussion and they reached an agreement as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to how he and other -- I'm sorry, as to how he would operate on the -- on the ground. And this operation, he says, didn't actually take place as discussed. But I find the meeting, the discussion, and the agreement on further action significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to ask you about another Crisis Staff head who took some military role. Tab 157, which is master tab 417. This is an intercepted conversation between Nedeljko Prstojevic and a Miroslav Gagovic on the 23rd of May, 1992. Before we play that, can you direct us to where the excerpt you want to talk about begins?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It begins on page 2 in the English, eight boxes up from the bottom, Prstojevic saying, "however, these people should know." And I will find it -- it begins at the very bottom of the B/C/S 04014074, the very last box and onto the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we'll play that one now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: However, these people should know about the Ilidza policy. Milosav GAGOVIC: Yes. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We have a sort of a big, the highest municipality. Milosav GAGOVIC: Certainly. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We have our policy in the area of Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Certainly. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Our policy in relation to refugees from Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: All the Serbs, men, women, children, adults will be accepted by Ilidza. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: And shall be accommodated. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Accommodation, food and the rest. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Secondly, no Muslim shall be allowed to leave Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Sorry? Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We shall not allow the Muslims to leave Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: ... the same number of the Serbs. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Because due to ... policy I accepted to perform ... Serbian people. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we hear that passage again, please, thank you? "Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: I have accepted it and took it in writing. I also told the press centre to register our views for the history. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK, Nedjo. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Please, I heard about some negotiations. I heard that they were organising some new convoy. It will not pass through. Milosav GAGOVIC: You're absolutely right. You're commanding, you have control and that's it. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: It will not pass through."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard another voice in between, something about repeating a passage. Did I hear that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the French booth was listening to the B/C/S and was therefore not really able to hear very well this passage. Maybe we could hear it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear it again, and then I take it the French booth translates the English or ... I'm now on channel 5 so I now can.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would then be interpreting from English, because we cannot really hear the B/C/S very clearly, if you want to play it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will commence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: However, these people should know about the Ilidza policy. Milosav GAGOVIC: Yes. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We have a sort of big, the highest municipality. Milosav GAGOVIC: Certainly. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We have our policy in the area of Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Certainly. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Our policy in relation to refugees from Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: All the Serbs, men, women, children, adults will be accepted by Ilidza. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: And shall be accommodated. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Accommodation, food and the rest. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Secondly, no Muslim shall be allowed to leave Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Sorry? Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: We shall not allow the Muslims to leave Sarajevo. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: ... the same number of the Serbs. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Because due to ... policy I accepted to perform ... Serbian people. Milosav GAGOVIC: Fine. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: I have accepted it and took it in writing. I also told the press centre to register our views for the history. Milosav GAGOVIC: OK, Nedjo. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: Please, I heard about some negotiations. I heard that they are organising a new convoy. It will not pass through. Milosav GAGOVIC: You're absolutely right. You are commanding, you have control and that's it. Nedeljko PRSTOJEVIC: It will not pass through."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I admire the speed at which you are able to translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, any comment on that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was struck here by the army commander because Gagovic was at this time acting as commander of the 4th Corps Sarajevo, saying to the commander of the Crisis Staff, "you are commanding, you have control." He is acknowledging Prstojevic's authority in his municipality, and also very indicative of the communications that a commander of the Crisis Staff calls the army commander, says "I'm not going to let a convoy through," and the army commander says, "you've set the policy," and is accepting that. It doesn't mean that Prstojevic is actually commanding the army per se, but that the army is acknowledging -- the word "command" obviously has some weight in the military terminology, so he's acknowledging the authority of the Crisis Staff in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next two tabs I think you put in for purposes of identifying the speakers to that conversation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Prstojevic is the president of the Crisis Staff of Ilija, and Gagovic as commander -- acting commander of the 4th Corpse.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's tab 158, master tab 326, regarding Prstojevic; tab 159, master tab 437 regarding Gagovic. Let me go to tab 160 in the presentation, master tab 174. Can you tell us what that document is and what you wanted to show from there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the government session of the 21st of May, 1992. We have seen it before on the question of support to Crisis Staffs. Here, I would draw your attention to page 3 of the translation, about two-thirds of the way down. And in the original, on page 3, that is, 01245324, the fifth item down. In the original, there is a blank, as indicated in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is there a corresponding blank in the original?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a corresponding blank in the original. The government has decided "to bring the decision on" something, the something "of Crisis Staffs as the military was taking over the defence and to create the conditions for work of regular institutions." As we know -- as we saw earlier, at the next session of the government, they do explicitly say to abolish Crisis Staffs. That would be consistent with the phrasing here, because they're saying, since the army is taking over defence, this is the point I wanted to bring your attention to here, they're doing something to Crisis Staffs. As we know, at the next session they decide it should be abolished, so I think it's a reasonable assumption here to say that that's what they're saying, because the army is taking over defence. This is the 19th of May. As we know, at the 12th of May Assembly session, the army -- the establishment of the VRS was announced. It was a formal decision on the establishment on the 19th of May. So two days later, after the VRS has been established, they're noting that the army is taking over defence. And as we know, they took steps at this time to abolish Crisis Staffs, which I think is indicative of the role the Crisis Staffs had until this point in defence. Now they have an army, the army is taking over defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me follow it up, then -- you mentioned this but we'll show it, presentation tab 161, master tab --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, they did -- they are there. I apologise. I didn't realise we'd be seeing that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- master tab 107, I think, is the point you were trying to make, that two days later --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just to say that blank was probably similar to the word "abolish". We don't know what the blank is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you direct us to where we are in this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was item 4 -- this is the minutes of the 23rd of May of the government session, item 4. We have seen this in the various presidential decisions and instructions. Just to point out that one of the processes going on at this time, in addition to forming the other legal organs, was the formation of the army. And Crisis Staffs were to be -- to give up their role, although, as we'll see, they maintained close contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next is presentation tab 162, master tab 255. Again, this is the combat-readiness report. And was there an excerpt from here that you wanted to talk about in connection with this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, the army itself gives a good description of this process. On page 11 in the translation, I believe it's 11 -- the number is a little cut off. This is -- in the B/C/S, it's 00607349, the fourth paragraph. It's the first paragraph on page -- in the English translation. It says that the second period in the establishment of the army came after -- was the establishment of the Main Staff in May, and then the next sentence: "By a decision of the Presidency of Republika Srpska of 15 May [sic] 1992 on the establishment, organisation, formation and command of the army of Republika Srpska, the organised life and combat operations of the army of Republika Srpska actually started, which, by a decision of the commander of the Main Staff of 16 June, 1992, was directed to pursue the basic strategic interests of the war of the Serbian people." So the army, as we saw from this and previous excerpts, similarly sees various stages in the development of the army. From the SDS-formed units to the Crisis Staffs commanding the first infantry units, to the army up and running, really, by 15 June here, it says the organised life and combat operations actually started. So those time periods are important to bear in mind when thinking about the question of Crisis Staff command of the army. It's also interesting, the last phrase in that paragraph, that the army was directed to pursue the basic strategic interests, which could be a reference to the strategic objectives. It's similar language.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In connection with that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, may I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, by reading, you said the 15th of May, but I take it that you wanted to read the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies if I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go to presentation tab 163, master tab 264. And to follow up on the point you were making about the strategic objectives, you referred to the strategic objectives of the Serbian people as announced in the --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 12th of May session. We'll see that again in the case studies, another indication of how these strategic objectives were communicated to the ground. But we see an example here at the minutes of a meeting of the command of the 1st Partizan Brigade with presidents of municipalities in their zone of responsibility, dated the 14th of May. So two days after the 12th of May Assembly session, after the declaration of the establishment of the army, the commander of the 1st Brigade meets with the political leaders of the municipalities. Present at the meeting, we see, item 1, Colonel Galic; item 2, Colonel Basar; item 5, president of the Kljuc municipal assembly, Jovo Banjac. He was also acting at this time as president of the Kljuc Crisis Staff. Similarly, item 6, the president of Sipovo municipal assembly, Radislav Djukic, was at this time president of the Crisis Staff of Sipovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And at this meeting on the 14th of May, 1992, what were the items discussed? Or is there one you want to bring to our attention?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, particular attention, on page 3 in the translation, also page 3 in the B/C/S, that is, 00421535. The president of the Mrkonjic Grad municipal assembly, who was also a deputy at the national assembly, presents the conclusions from the meeting held in Banja Luka. I take this to be a reference to the Banja Luka, that is -- Assembly session, the 12th of May Assembly session that was held in Banja Luka, because the conclusions he presents are all consistent with the conclusions of the 12 May Assembly session: To name the armed forces of Krajina - as it is put down here - to name them the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and describes how members of the JNA from the area will be members of the VRS; the land forces, air force will be developed. He presents the strategic goals formulated at the meeting in Banja Luka. Number 1, "There must be a state separation of the three national communities; 2, Krajina must be connected with Serbia along the right bank of the Sava River; 3, creation of a corridor along the Drina river valley; 4 establishing borders from the Una river to the Neretva river; 5, it was said that Sarajevo must either be divided or razed to the ground; 6, examine the possibility of access to the sea for the Serbian Republic." So it is interesting that we see the decisions of the Assembly being conveyed to presidents of municipalities and army leaders, and they are meeting together to discuss the transformation of the army. And these strategic goals are similarly being transmitted to this municipal level and to the army. I would note that one of the strategic objectives that we do know is formulated at the 12 May Assembly session is not specified here -- oh, it is, the Drina, I'm sorry. I thought the Drina was missing, but it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do have a question about the formulation of the objectives here as compared to how they were stated in the Assembly. In particular, with regard to number 5, Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 5 is the different one. In the Assembly, there is no mention of it being razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the attendees at this meeting is Colonel Galic --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- who later was involved in the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is one of the attendees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, Mr. -- in 5, I see in the translation, "double-underlined" in the original. That must be another original. We came across that several times, because there's no double-underlining, Mr. Hannis, in 5 of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree. I see what you're talking about. It does have the same ERN number that 01106533 is purporting to be a translation of, so I would assume that that was from a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, as a matter of fact, that it is -- yes, it could be, but perhaps there are several originals. Could you please check that? It's somewhere in the back of my mind, but I must be careful that I'm not mixing up cases, that there are various versions of this document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will make a note and check on that and report back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps if it sounds not familiar to you, to consult colleagues of yours who have been dealing with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder at this moment, because I wasn't quite sure what the timetable was intended to be this morning, I did have one practical suggestion, unless Your Honours already had a -- something in mind, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware that many of you have been in this courtroom when we had not yet started, so I intended to have a break from 10 minutes past 11.00 until 11.30. That would be a short break, 20 minutes. Then go on after the break until 12.30, and then have another break for 20 minutes until 12.50, and then finished by 13.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have absolutely no problem with that. The tiny practical suggestion, Your Honour, was this: That the timetable would enable, Your Honours, in fact to have a single break. If Your Honours broke at 11.35 and broke until 12.15, we can manage with one break and then go to the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I considered that. But since some of those who are assisting us were in court all the time, waiting, on the suggestion of Madam Registrar, I decided that we would have two short breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour, then obviously we'll accept and are content with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have any other questions about that. Did you have any other comments --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was -- I'm sorry, I'll just repeat that this is also consistent with what we saw in the description of the role of the deputies, that they are the ones to go to the municipality and convey the decisions of the Assembly. And we see this in practice here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I would like to go to presentation tab 164, master tab 205. This is an intercepted telephone conversation between General Mladic and Colonel Gagovic and Professor Unkovic on the 13th of May. Can you direct us to which portion of that conversation we'll be listening to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the English translation, about two-thirds of the way down the first page, starting with Mladic saying, "This is General Mladic here." And in the B/C/S, it's the second box from the bottom on the first page of the B/C/S, 03220204.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll play that one now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Hannis --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's not suddenly my favorite subject, but in the English version, I find parts emphasised by underlying, whereas I do not find that in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honour. I didn't notice that. I will provide a clean copy to the Court and counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Let's now listen to the intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mladic: This is General Mladic here. How are you? Unkovic: Welcome to our house. Mladic: Thank you. May we have luck in our endeavour. Unkovic: May great Lord help you. Mladic: Tell me, do you ... Let me first tell you about what you're interested in. Unkovic: Yes? Mladic: Koljevic will come ... Koljevic ... Unkovic: Mmm. Mladic: ... Ostojic and myself will represent our side. Unkovic: Excellent. Mladic: There. So there is no need for you to have a representative as Ilidza. You can, however, join us and let us know about your problems there, if it is safe for you to come. The most important thing now is that the military formations, no matter who they belong to, be put under the command of the 4th Corps HQ, to Gagovic. Unkovic: Yes? Mladic: All this. Units shall be brought to strength, formed, organised and everything must be all right. Unkovic: Excellent. Mladic: Have you understood me? Unkovic: Yes. Mladic: I'll give you further instructions when we get together. Unkovic: Excellent. Mladic: There. Unkovic: One more question. Mladic: Yes? Unkovic: We have some Arkan's men here. Mladic: Yes? Unkovic: Are they under our command? Mladic: All of them are. All under arms are under my command, if they want to stay alive that is. Unkovic: Excellent. Excellent. Mladic: So, all those shall be under our command. No one shall do things on their own, and the five-day cease-fire must be observed. Unkovic: Yes. Mladic: But, in case they attack you, approach you, then you will destroy them. Unkovic: Of course. Mladic: There. Unkovic: Sure thing."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any comment on that one, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would note the date here, the 13th of May, the day after the announcement of the establishment of the VRS. Unkovic identifies himself as from the Crisis Staff from Ilidza, and Ratko Mladic addresses him directly, saying that units shall be filled with men, formed, organised, and put under the command of the 4th Corps, Gagovic. That is, again, consistent with the process of the establishment of the army. And also the question of Arkan's men, Mladic insisting that all -- anyone with a gun, even the paramilitaries, such as Arkan's men, are under "our command." Unkovic says "our command," indicating the united command. I don't think he's claiming here his Crisis Staff authority, but rather, We're all on to the same side, they're under our command. The direct contact itself is significant; that a member of the Crisis Staff is talking directly with Mladic. Mladic -- the first subject on whether Koljevic will come and Ostojic's question of negotiations about the airport, and Mladic is saying, You can come and let us know your problems. So clear contacts between Crisis Staff and military leadership, and a commonality of purpose here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next one is another intercept of about the same length, so perhaps this would be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is 10 minutes past 11.00, so perhaps before we go to the next one, we'll have a break of 20 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I was ready to go next to presentation tab 165, master tab 266. This is another intercepted conversation, Your Honours, between Ratko Mladic and a Glisa Simanic on the 25th of May, 1992. Ms. Hanson, could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you direct the Court to where we're beginning.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we're beginning almost at the beginning. The third line of the conversation on page of the translation, and similarly, the third box on the first page of the B/C/S. I would note before we begin that Glisa Simanic was a member of the Crisis Staff of Trnovo, and when we get to the Trnovo Crisis Staff, we'll see a quite lot about Glisa Simanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll play that one now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Simanic Glisa: The line was interrupted. Mladic Ratko: Who are you? Simanic Glisa: Glisa Simanic. Mladic Ratko: From Trnovo? Simanic Glisa: Yes. Mladic Ratko: This is General Mladic here. Simanic Glisa: How are you? Mladic Ratko: Excellent. What's going on over there? Simanic Glisa: Well, we have a ... some movement by their forces from the direction of Konjic. Mladic Ratko: Where are they headed? Simanic Glisa: They're headed ... a convoy of trucks has set out. We think they could only be ... Mladic Ratko: I asked where they were headed. I didn't ask you to think. Where are they headed? Simanic Glisa: From the direction of Konjic towards the village of Lukomir. Mladic Ratko: Lukomir? And then? Simanic Glisa: Yes. Then towards Sabici and Trnovo. Mladic Ratko: All right. And then by way of Lukomir and Sabici? Simanic Glisa: Yes, yes. This convoy is on the move now. Mladic Ratko: On the move? How many of them are there? Simanic Glisa: We don't know that. Mladic Ratko: And who ... do you have the means to stop this convoy? Simanic Glisa: No, because this is ... Mladic Ratko: Well, of course not, because you waste time in Trnovo sitting in bars. Comrade, form a group of ten to twenty soldiers, intercept the convoy and capture them. Do you understand me? Simanic Glisa: Listen ... Mladic Ratko: You listen to me. Did you hear what I ordered you? Simanic Glisa: Yes. Mladic Ratko: That's what you will do. Find a way to penetrate through there and set up an ambush somewhere in those woods, wait for them, check them out, capture them and fucking chase them away. And don't give me that bullshit like we went here or we went there. You're not reconnaissance but infantry. Is the road towards Dobro Polje and Kijevo negotiable? Simanic Glisa: Barely. Mladic Ratko: Why? Simanic Glisa: We heard some kind of explosion down at the dam. We've just sent a reconnaissance to check it out. It seems they have mined the road down there. Mladic Ratko: Never mind. Let them mine it. Anything else? Simanic Glisa: We don't have any other interesting information for now. Mladic Ratko: You see what it's about? Is it you or them who controls Trnovo? Simanic Glisa: It's us. Mladic Ratko: You have Trnovo under control? Simanic Glisa: Yes. Mladic Ratko: Excellent. So, one can get through to Trnovo? Simanic Glisa: From the direction of Dobro Polje. Mladic Ratko: From the direction of Dobro Polje? Simanic Glisa: No problem. Mladic Ratko: Excellent. Check that thing down there and you'll have to get in contact with those ... I'm offering them peace if they want peace. And tell them, those Muslims there, that they had better not start anything because they'll go to hell. Simanic Glisa: I understand. Mladic Ratko: And whenever they want it I'll come to talk. Simanic Glisa: I understand. Mladic Ratko: There. I will designate a place for our meeting. You just get in contact with them sometime today and let me know. I will come and tell everyone where we'll meet. Simanic Glisa: I understand."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And your comment on that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, Glisa Simanic is a member of the Trnovo Crisis Staff, and here he's getting orders from Ratko Mladic. The word he says -- is translated as "I understand it," it means that "razumijem" but it's also the military equivalent of "yes, sir," what you say when you're given an order. If you hear the intonation, it sounds very much like yes, sir. It's also interesting here, Mladic is expecting further contact with Simanic, authorising him to negotiate in his name, talk to the Muslims, get back to me, we'll arrange a meeting. And, as the order makes clear, ordering him to take military action to seize a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next tab, presentation tab 166, master tab 44, is a document you put in to show who Simanic was.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We'll see this document again in the Trnovo case study, but it's notable here that he is -- it's minutes of the Trnovo SDS municipal board, 27 December 1991. Simanic is named as coordinator for crisis situations. And we see him speaking to Mladic in a moment of apparent crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have a translation question. It appears in the English in that document. The name is Glisa Simanic. I note that the original document is a handwritten document. Do you know from other information that it should be Glisa Simanic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We will see that name in many of the Trnovo documents, and the handwriting is not the clearest. But perhaps the interpreters could confirm. It's in the original at 02280490 that it appears to be more Simanic than Simonic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll take your word for it. We don't have it in Sanction to put it up for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I can put it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can see it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Simanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I'd like to go and ask you regarding now, after the formation of the VRS in May 1992, did you see a change in how the Crisis Staffs were interacting with the military?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see continued close coordination and contacts with the military in this time period. As the military structures are being set up and empowered, we see more assertion, naturally, of militaries having their own command structure and command authority over the units. But we see continued close contacts, which is part of the coordinating functions of the Crisis Staff that we saw in the normative documents, that coordination of defence was one of their principle roles. And we see this borne out. Even as the military has their own command structures, they are in close contact with the municipal authorities, in this case the Crisis Staff and the War Presidencies --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's reflected in the next set of documents?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me take you to tab 167, master tab 201.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Petrovac on the 10th of June, 1992. I would just note here that a representative of the command is here. I take that to be the military unit there. It's clear in other items what kind of military -- it's a little vague right here, but we'll see other documents that make it clear they're talking about military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And tab number 168, which is master tab 267. Tell us what that is and what you want to refer us to.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could put the highlighted version on the ELMO, because this binder does not seem to have the updated translation. If I could just do that. This is minutes of the meeting of the Kotor Varos Crisis Staff from the 6th of July, 1992. Under item 2 in the minutes, then number 2 within that: "It was agreed to replace the municipal Crisis Staff with a War Presidency that would comprise the municipal assembly president, the executive committee chairman, the secretary of the secretariat for national defence, public security station chief, secretary of the secretariat for the economy, and the commander of the largest unit carrying out combat operations within the municipality." Notable here that the date is the 6th of July, so we can see that the Crisis Staff does -- is replaced with a War Presidency, but much later than the decision we saw issued on the 31st of May. But the makeup is similar and is consistent with the idea of coordination of defence and other municipal organs, so specifying the commander of the largest unit in the municipality is to be a member of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And actually, at that time in July, wouldn't it have been, according to the series of documents, we have going from Crisis Staff to War Presidency to War Commission, it should have been a War Commission --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the documents are written, yes, it would appear. But we have seen so many War Presidencies at this time that it's not surprising -- it is quite consistent with the pattern we see, that they are not always War Commission, often War Presidencies, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, let me take you to presentation tab 169, master tab 141.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document we've seen before, but I just wanted, in this case, to point out, as I did at the -- first time I showed it. I don't mean to bore you with repetition. It's conclusions of the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most on the 30th of May, but I wanted to note here that under item 10, Branko Basara, commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, is a member of the Crisis Staff. If you'll recall, he was also at that meeting of the 14th of May that we looked at before the break. So, again, the military commander is included in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, I'd like to show you tab 170 in the presentation, master tab 273. This is from the command of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the 1st of July, of the 1st Krajina Corps command. I would take you to the top of page 2 in the translation; in the B/C/S, on the second page, 01029804, the fourth paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what is General Talic directing?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Talic here says that: "Zone commanders shall establish personal contact with organs of authorities who are duty-bound to perform the tasks for which they are responsible. The latter cannot command units located on the territory of the municipality." As I said, this is the 1st of July, so we would expect here, according to the army's account of its establishment, that by now it is -- its actual life, operational life, has begun. So it is consistent with that pattern that Talic is now saying that regional -- zone commanders should establish contact with the municipal authorities -- here it says simply organs of authorities, but it appears to be referring to the municipalities, and that those organs of authority cannot command units, indicative, perhaps, of the fact that some did command before the establishment of the army. Now the army is asserting its command authority over units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And tab 171 in the presentation, master tab 284, is this a reflection of at least one Crisis Staff recognising that difference, that now there is an army?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 4 to 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what document is this from?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the bulletin of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos. This is issue number 3 of the 26th of June, 1992. You'll recall that we saw -- we looked at issue number 6 yesterday. Yes, at the bottom of the second page in the B/C/S, 00416213. At the very bottom of page 4: "The Crisis Staff concluded that it does not have the right to interfere in the professional work of the police and army, nor does it wish to do so. But it does request that they themselves undertake security and the creation of conditions for full security on the municipal territory." So this is a Crisis Staff that is distancing itself from command of those units, saying it's a job for professionals. But you'll recall that we did see in Kotor Varos, they named the commander of the largest unit as a member of the War Presidency, when it was established. This phrasing, you will recall, is also consistent with Djeric's instructions of 26 April 1992, which said, prevent any interference in the command of the TO and the army because that is -- of the police, because that is a job for professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go to tab 172 in the presentation, master binder 124 -- master tab 124. This is an article from a publication called Glas. Can you tell the Court what Glas was?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a daily newspaper in the RS, I believe from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what is the excerpt you wanted to bring to the Court's attention?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an article from the 7th of July, 1992, from a press conference held by Colonel Bogdan Subotic, Defence Minister of the Serbian Republic. He is saying that it is -- he's informing the public of the government decree on disbanding Crisis Staffs in all municipalities where conditions exist for the operation of legal authorities. In particular, the third paragraph of the translation; in the original it's on page 00951907, it's the third paragraph of the black box text. It's a newspaper article -- newspaper front page, and there's a lot of articles, but the last one on the front page. "'Experience,' says Subotic, 'so far shows that the jurisdictions of Crisis Staffs and military organs were not always clearly delineated, so minor misunderstandings occurred.'".

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to another topic regarding the military and the Crisis Staffs. Now that the army has been created and there appears to be some recognition that that's a separate professional body, did that end relationships between Crisis Staffs and the military?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. Relations remained very close, because the Crisis Staffs continued to play an essential role in supporting the military units in their municipalities and in coordinating, sharing information with the military leadership, as we saw. The military presence was a constant on many -- most Crisis Staffs, it's a constant pattern we see. And this whole question of the support is something we see throughout the time period. I've been trying to describe the various phases and variations in the question of command and orders to units, but the question of supporting units is something we see consistently throughout the time period and throughout the different municipalities. So we can put aside more complicated issues of variations and look at the consistent coordination, support.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next series of documents, there's some examples of that support?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first two are just a few of -- just two of very numerous, numerous examples of mobilisation. This is one of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first one would be presentation tab 173, master tab 250.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The announcement of the Crisis Staff of Vogosca, dated the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Announcing general mobilisation. I would also note here that the municipal Crisis Staff is using the seal, the stamp, of the SDS municipal office for its documents. Another indication of the overlap. But this is one of many mobilisation orders, announcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Another example of that, presentation tab 174, master tab 418.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from the Crisis Staff of Zvornik. As I mentioned before, Zvornik had, in the first few days of the conflict, a Crisis Staff which then formed a provisional government. We don't have them co-existing. But this is one of the few documents from the Crisis Staff of Zvornik. Again, an order on mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, let me show you presentation tab 175, master tab 272. This is a report from the Krajina Corps. Could you direct the Court to the excerpt you want to discuss?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's at the bottom of page 2, the last full paragraph -- the last paragraph on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the original, I'm just looking, it's on page 3 in the B/C/S, that is, 00900794. And in the middle of the paragraph: "In future, the commands of regiments, brigades --" I'm sorry, forgive me. "In future, the commands of regiments, brigades, and independent battalions must forward individual applications to the municipal and communal Crisis Staffs because they are able to organise supplies, housing and welfare benefits for the families of conscripts." Just a notation of the army's view of the role of Crisis Staffs after the formation of the army structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, presentation tab 176, master tab 216. This is a document dated the 2nd of June, 1992, from the Bosanski Samac Crisis Staff, and another variation of support.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just indications of the kinds of support a Crisis Staff gave. A decision of the Samac Crisis Staff of the 2nd of June. Under item 1, the Crisis Staff instructs the executive committee to purchase 500 uniforms for the needs of the special purpose battalion of the VRS which is stationed in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, tab number 177 in the presentation, master tab 147.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a decision of the Crisis Staff of Ilidza, dated the 10th of May, 1992, saying, "Regarding the issue of the transfer of soldiers and officers from the JNA to the army of the Republic of Serbian --" this is before the actual establishment of the VRS. At the top of the page 2 in the translation, under item 2 in the B/C/S original: "The Crisis Staff and the Assembly of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza takes upon itself the responsibility for caring for the families of the Serbian soldiers and officers during the war, and for making arrangements for their housing and employment after the war." It also promises them other benefits and security. So just an indication of the kind of support the Crisis Staffs offered militaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And next in the series, tab 178 in the presentation, master tab 215. This is from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an interesting document. It is a report dated the 17th of June, 1992, of the logistics base of Cirkin Polje of the Prijedor Crisis Staff. And it's reporting basically on the vehicles and other resources of this logistics base. I would bring your attention to page 1, the preamble, which says that: "Pursuant to the decision on the general and public mobilisation, the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor and the order of the commander of the Serbian army Territorial Defence staff of Prijedor municipality, Major Slobodan Kuruzovic, troops and equipment were mobilised in the logistical support staff." You can see that the Crisis Staff decision was needed for the setting up of this support staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is there another excerpt?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's an interesting excerpt on page 5 in the translation, which I will find now in the original. This is on page 5 in the original, P0008408. It notes in the first paragraph of the translation, top of page 5, that is -- I'm sorry, first paragraph on page 5, that they've sent a report to the Crisis Staff and garrison command on sending supplies to other staffs. Then the first full paragraph: "We would like to point out that from the day of the takeover and the establishment of the logistics section in the Serbian army TO staff in Prijedor up to 10 June 1992, in addition to many sanitation and medical measures, we have also provided the weapons and ammunition for sector staffs and secured and delivered about 100.000 meals to members of the police and Serbian army TO units." The next paragraph mentions accepting the restructuring of the army in accordance with the decision of the Assembly of 12 May 1992. And then the next paragraph, saying that a meeting of 10 June 1992 -- "A meeting of the Crisis Staff of the Serb municipality of Prijedor and the garrison command, held on 10 June 1992, attended by Major Slobodan Kuruzovic, commander of the Serbian army staff, as well as --" it names some other commanders. "All instructions given by the garrison command and the Crisis Staff relating to the transformation of the Territorial Defence into the army of the Serbian Republic of BH were accepted. With this in mind, we have taken a series of measures and steps in cooperation with the garrison command logistics with the goal of providing full material support to members of Serbian army units and police officers in the municipality area, and providing food supplies to the prisons in Keraterm and Omarska."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the last tab in binder number 4. We're ready to hand up presentation binder number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I think in the -- this next binder, we also have a couple more examples of Crisis Staff support for the military.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll get to that in a moment while we change binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I put one question in relation to the last binder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was a report of the Prijedor municipality Crisis Staff, the logistics base in Cirkin Polje. To whom was it addressed, and to whom was it sent? Where was it found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was found, I believe, with other documents of the Prijedor Crisis Staff, but it is -- I don't have it in front of me, I can't check the internal evidence, but there's no addressee, obviously, there. We do see many summaries of reports of the work -- several summaries of reports of work of the Crisis Staff to their municipal assemblies. But the date of this is earlier than -- I believe we see the Prijedor Assembly meeting in July. I don't take it to be then. I can't say from the face of that document to see whom it is addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be a possibility for you to find out, I don't know whether this is the only version of this report that exists or whether it has been found in other places as well, to find out to whom it was sent, even if not addressed, and who might have received it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will look into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now we're in presentation binder number 5, and the first tab, presentation 179, master tab 219. Still talking about examples of support.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the conclusions of the provisional government of Zvornik of -- dated the 4th of June, 1992, but it shows the provisional government setting the pay for members of a Territorial Defence, saying that they will be paid by the -- under Article 4, paid by the accounting service of the provisional government.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: So an indication of the government providing the pay for what they called Serbian Army Territorial Defence. In article 1, it's explicated Serbian Army and Territorial Defence, indicating in May that this is a period of transition. There's different units, different names. The provisional government is paying them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And finally, in connection with this series of documents, presentation tab 180, master tab 220.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- it's called a recapitulation of transactions from the cashiers of the Crisis Staff. It is found with other documents of the Vogosca Crisis Staff. Although I do not see anything here specifying that, I took it to mean the Vogosca Crisis Staff because it's among their own documents. Under item 1, I would just note, of their income -- I'm sorry, under item 2, the outgoing payments, forgive me. If you look at the bottom of the page, of the total outgoing payments of 22 million dinars, 14 million went to soldiers' daily allowance. So the bulk of their budget was soldiers' pay. It indicates the extent to which Crisis Staffs devoted themselves to supporting soldiers. Again, to give you a rough order of magnitude, according to the official exchange rate of the 1st of June - this is only rough, but to give you a rough idea - 22 million is about 70.000 U.S. dollars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That concludes the documents I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I have a question. How were these Crisis Staffs budgeted? I mean, where did they find that money? Where did that money come from? Who decided what amount they would get? Who decided how the money would be allocated between the various Crisis Staffs? I would be grateful if you could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this document may be able to answer it. If we look at the top item, their income, the first line, it says "aid" and then it says "SRBiH". It's translated "as aid to Socialist Republic", but I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. think that's a confusion, because in this case, the SR -- the S is more likely to refer to Serb Republic. And it says "aid to" in English but if I could just show the interpreters what the original is, it simply says "aid" and then "SRBiH" could also be in B/C/S "aid from." We saw in the accounts of the Ilijas Crisis Staff that the bulk of their income came from the government of the Serb Republic of BH.
